{"bacDaoTao":{"id":2,"ma":"DH","ten":{"vi":"Đại học","en":"Undergraduate"}},"loaiMonHoc":{"id":21,"ma":"CN","ten":{"vi":"Chuyên Ngành"}},"mucTieuMonHoc":{"vi":"


Trang bị cho sinh viên những kiến thức cơ bản về  vật liệu polyme dẫn điện, khả năng lựa chọn, tổng hợp và áp dụng những polyme dẫn điện cho những ứng dụng thích hợp như là pin năng lượng mặt trời nền hữu cơ, transistor hữu cơ, sensor, ứng dụng cho màn hình OLED…


","en":"

 Deeply understanding principles of   conjugated polymer fundamentals and rationally choosing, synthesis of conjugated polymer, and application of conjugated polymer in organic solar cell, organic field effect transistor, sensor, OLED display…

"},"noiDungTomTatMonHoc":{"vi":"

Giới thiệu về một số polyme dẫn điện phổ biến, cơ chế dẫn điện của conducting polymer, phương pháp tổng hợp monomer dẫn điện, phương pháp tổng hợp polymer dẫn điện bao gồm phương pháp polycondensation (step growth polymerization), phương pháp GRIM (chain growth polymerization). Lựa chọn và sử dụng polyme dẫn điện trong những ứng dụng pin mặt trời nền hữu cơ, transistor hữu cơ, sensor, màn hình OLED và những thiết bị quang điện khác

","en":"

 Introduction of popular conjuagted polymers, conducting mechanism of conjuagted polymers, the method for synthesis of conducting monomer then the lecture will give conjuated polymer polymerizations include polycondensation (step growth polymerization), GRIM method (chain growth polymerization). Design and selection the conjugated polymers for application of organic solar cells, organic field effect transistor, sensor, OLED displays and optic-electronic devices.

"},"taiLieuHocTap":{"vi":"

[1] Handbook of Conducting Polymers Third Edition, Conjugated polymers : theory, synthesis, properties, and characterization. Edited by Terje A. Skotheim and John R. Reynolds. CRC Press Taylor & Francis Group 6000 Broken Sound Parkway NW, Suite 300 Boca Raton, FL 33487-2742

[2] Organic Photochemistry and Photophysics. edited by Vaidhyanathan Ramamurthy University of Miami Miami, Florida. le-tex publishing services oHG, Leipzig, Germany.

[3] Handbook of Advanced Electronic and Photonic Materials and Devices. Edited by Hari Singh Nalwa, M.Sc, Ph.D. Stanford Scientific Corporation Los Angeles, California, USA

[4] Organic Field-Effect Transistors, Editor Brian J. Thompson University of Rochester Rochester, New York. CRC Press is an imprint of the Taylor & Francis Group.

[5] Luminescent Materials and Applications. Edited by Adrian Kitai 2008 John Wiley & Sons.

[6] Thiophenes (Best Synthetic Methods). Edited by : Salo Gronowitz and Anna-Britta Hörnfeldt, Elsevier, 2004.

[7] Functional Synthetic Receptors. Editors by Prof. Dr. Thomas Schrader Philipps-Universität Marburg Fachbereich Chemie Hans-Meerwein-Strasse 35032 Marburg Germany, Prof. Dr. Andrew D. Hamilton Yale University Department of Chemistry Sterling Chemistry Laboratory 225 Prospect Street New Haven, CT 06520, USA.

[8] Self-Doped Conducting Polymers. Editors by Michael S. Freund and Bhavana A. Deore Department of Chemistry, University of Manitoba, Canada. John Wiley & Sons Ltd, The Atrium, Southern Gate, Chichester, West Sussex PO19 8SQ, England.

[9] Synthesis of Conjugated Polymers for Organic Solar Cell Applications. Editors by Yen-Ju Cheng, Sheng-Hsiung Yang, and Chain-Shu Hsu. Department of Applied Chemistry, National Chiao Tung University, 1001 Ta Hsueh Road, Hsin-Chu 30049, Taiwan.

[10] Handbook of Thiophene-based Materials: Applications in Organic Electronics and Photonics Editors by IGOR F. PEREPICHKA Centre for Materials Science University of Central Lancashire Preston, UK DMITRII and F. PEREPICHKA Department of Chemistry McGill University Montreal, Quebec, Canada.

-thực hiện đầy đủ các bài tập trên lớp và bài tập về nhà, tham gia buổi tham quan phòng thí nghiệm để trang bị thêm kiến thức thực tiễn

Giới thiệu
1.1 Ưu điểm của vật liệu polymer dẫn điện

1.3 Ảnh hưởng của quá trình truyền điện tích đến tính chất quang của polymer dẫn điện

1.1. Advantages of conducting polymers
1.2. Electronic couplings in organic semiconductors
